title: Langues de Chat (Cat's Tongue Biscuits)
summary: Light, crisp little French biscuits piped into slim fingers, with golden edges and a delicate, buttery bite.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
piping bag with a 1 cm plain nozzle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large egg whites, at room temperature

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), with a shelf in the middle, for at least 20 minutes before baking. These thin biscuits bake quickly, so the oven needs to be fully up to temperature from the start.

steps.title: Cream the butter
steps.text: Beat the very soft butter with the icing sugar, salt and vanilla for 1-2 minutes until smooth and creamy. Starting with really soft butter means it blends evenly without needing to beat in excess air.

steps.title: Add egg whites gradually
steps.text: Add the egg whites a little at a time, beating well after each addition. Using room-temperature whites and adding them gradually stops the mixture splitting; if it does curdle slightly, beat in a spoonful of the flour to bring it back together.

steps.title: Fold in flour and zest
steps.text: Fold in the flour, and the lemon zest if using, just until smooth. Folding rather than beating at this stage keeps the batter light enough to pipe cleanly.

steps.title: Pipe the fingers
steps.text: Pipe the batter into fingers about 7-8cm long, spacing them 5cm apart, as they spread considerably in the oven. Tap the tray firmly on the worktop to settle the piped lines and release any air bubbles.

steps.title: Bake until edged golden
steps.text: Bake one tray at a time for 6-9 minutes, until the edges are golden brown but the centres are still pale. This contrast between crisp, browned edges and a soft pale middle is exactly what gives langues de chat their delicate bite.

steps.title: Cool and crisp
steps.text: Leave on the tray for 1 minute, then lift onto a wire rack. They firm up and turn properly crisp only as they cool, so don't judge them straight from the oven.

tips: Make sure the egg whites are truly at room temperature before adding them, as cold whites are the main reason the batter splits.
Pipe evenly sized fingers so they all bake in the same time - uneven piping means some will be underdone while others overbake.
Leave plenty of space between the piped lines; a common mistake is crowding the tray, which causes the biscuits to spread into one another.
Watch closely near the end of baking, as the thin edges can go from golden to overly dark within a minute.
Bake one tray at a time in the centre of the oven for the most even colour.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 4 days. They don't freeze well baked, as the thin, crisp texture doesn't survive thawing.
